title: Fly over Skardu: Indus, Kharpocho and Satpara
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: In Gilgit-Baltistan, at nearly two thousand four hundred and thirty metres, lies Skardu, the capital of Baltistan.
Let's fly in from the west, along the wide, sandy valley.
Below us is the Indus River, one of the great rivers of Asia.
Skardu stands where the Indus meets the Shigar River.
It is the gateway to the giants: K2, Broad Peak and the Gasherbrums are all reached from here.
On a rocky hill above the town stands Kharpocho Fort, built under the Maqpoon rulers, most famously Ali Sher Khan Anchan.
Its history goes back to the late fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, and it still watches over the Indus valley.
Now we turn south, to Satpara Lake, about nine kilometres from the city.
Satpara is Skardu's main source of drinking water, and it feeds Satpara Dam, which supplies water and electricity to the region.
Beyond it, the road climbs to the Deosai plains, home to brown bears and snow leopards.
The best time to visit is May to September. In winter, many roads and trails close.
